messages:
incident-bot: Pager alert: infer-usw-2 - multiple kubelet restarts detected on node inf-node-07. Pod restarts, 5xxs rising. Incident severity: P1
Ava (oncall): I’m on it. marking priority P1. starting triage — @Marta can you grab runtime logs for affected pods?
Marta (runtime): looking. preliminary... I see repeated "OOM when allocating tensor" in runtime logs on inf-runtime-52. Also nxdriver says "CUDA driver lost connection". grabbing full snippet
Marta (runtime): ```
2026-03-15T13:12:07Z runtime ERROR: cuda: driver lost device
2026-03-15T13:12:07Z runtime WARN: retrying init, attempt=1
2026-03-15T13:12:08Z runtime ERROR: process exit code 137 (OOM?)
```
Priya: metrics: 5xx rate across infer-usw is up from 0.2% to 4.8% last 10m. p95 latency jumped from 45ms to 980ms. CPU on other nodes spiking as pods reschedule. Graph: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abc123/infer-usw
Jordan: we should cordon/drain inf-node-07, then restart kubelet. I'll run commands, posting here so ops can revert if needed:
Jordan: ```
kubectl cordon inf-node-07
kubectl drain inf-node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl get pods -o wide | grep inf-runtime | grep inf-node-07
ssh root@inf-node-07 'systemctl restart kubelet'
```
Ava (oncall): go for it @Jordan. Also start scale-up on standby pool: set inference deployment replica +3 for 10m.
Jordan: scaled inference-pool-usw deployment +3 replicas (rollback scheduled in 15m). pods are scheduling onto inf-node-02/04.
Elias (support): CS ping: two customers reported increased latency in last 8m. CS ticket IDs: #CS-5421, #CS-5422. tagging customers with ETA 30m.
Marta (runtime): more logs — drivers updated ~1h ago on inf-node-07 (gpu-image:v2.3.4 -> v2.3.5). I suspect driver regression + existing memory pressure caused cuda resets.
Priya: inventory shows inf-node-07 has slightly lower free GPU memory before incident (memory fragmentation). Combined with runtime's new driver maybe triggers OOM on attach.
Jordan: I manually evicted the remaining inference pods from inf-node-07 and they're healthy on other nodes. kubelet still restarted twice in last 8m. Ops, can you reboot node if kubelet restart fails? @ops-bot
ops-bot: Enqueued reboot play: inf-node-07. ETA 4m.
Marta (runtime): while we stabilize, flip routing policy for production customers to model-variant:small-fp16 for 20m to reduce per-request GPU memory. Applying now.
Ava (oncall): applied routing fallback; traffic shifted ~65% to small-fp16. 5xx rate down to 1.2% in 5m. p95 latency 210ms.
Jordan: node reboot completed. kubelet came back but still logs show driver warnings. I'm going to cordon permanently until we validate driver image across fleet.
Jordan: `kubectl uncordon inf-node-07` — not until QA signs off. (keeping cordoned)
Marta (runtime): created a rollback play to revert gpu-image to v2.3.4 for inf-node-07. scheduling for maintenance window but can apply emergency revert now if oncall approves.
Ava (oncall): approve emergency revert. Marta, proceed and post status.
Marta (runtime): reverted driver image on inf-node-07; restarted runtime container. Post-revert checks: no cuda resets in last 3m, pod health restored.
Priya: metrics: 5xx at 0.4%, p95 60ms. CPU/GPU balance normalized. No further restarts for 10m.
Elias (support): updated customers: CS-5421/5422 notified, shared root-cause (kubelet restarts + driver regression causing cuda OOM), mitigation and ETA for postmortem.
Ava (oncall): nice work everyone. I’ll hand this to infra for follow-up driver validation and AM to coordinate postmortem. Handoff: @Jordan takes final oncall shift at 08:00 UTC.
Jordan: ack. I’ll own post-incident follow-ups: driver validation across infer-usw, add a canary check for new gpu-image deploys, and update autoscale thresholds to avoid overpacking.
incident-bot: Incident closed (P1 -> resolved) at ts=4332109950. runbook: https://runbook.internal/kubelet-flap-infer
Ava (oncall): postmortem owner assigned: Jordan. ETA to draft: 48h.
